solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Game which involves flinging small ferrets

blocks.note: hob is an old game of tossing stones at a coin balanced on a stick, also called hob
S is the usual abbreviation for small

explanation.surface: A cruel pastime of hurling little ferrets about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Game' looks like the definition, but the answer is the plural of the male ferret.
explanation.definitionFit: A hob is a male ferret, so the plural noun names several of the animals.

clue.text: Savage switch for Diana, say

blocks.note: a Hun is a barbarian, a savage
a switch is a hairpiece, a long lock or tress of hair

explanation.surface: A wild swap of roles for someone called Diana.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Switch' is not a change but a hairpiece.
explanation.definitionFit: Diana was the Roman goddess of the hunt, an example of a female hunter; 'say' marks the example.

clue.text: Blocking response in the matter of stringent sewer's product

blocks.note: in Chinese medicine bi is an obstruction of the flow of qi, a blocking response
as means in the capacity or manner of
a stringent rule is binding, strictly obligatory

explanation.surface: Talk of obstruction and strict rules dressed up as legal jargon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sewer' is one who sews, not a drain. Bi is an obscure term from Chinese medicine.
explanation.definitionFit: Bias binding is a strip of fabric cut on the cross grain, made by or used by someone who sews to finish edges.

clue.text: Laurel, for example, in drag wandered around Ireland

indicators.note: something said to be in drag is literally inside it, so one piece sits within the other

blocks.note: a drag is a sledge, something dragged along
the laurel is an example of a tree

explanation.surface: Laurel, of Laurel and Hardy, dressed as a woman and touring Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In drag' reads as cross-dressing, but drag is a sledge with the tree put inside it. 'Around Ireland' labels the definition as Irish usage.
explanation.definitionFit: Streel is an Irish verb meaning to wander aimlessly or trail about, so the past tense matches wandered.

clue.text: Scoundrel wallowing in self certainty

indicators.note: a creature wallowing in mud is surrounded by it, so one piece lies inside the other

blocks.note: seity is selfhood, the quality of being oneself
a cur is a contemptible man, a scoundrel

explanation.surface: A rogue lost in smug self-assurance.
explanation.walkthrough: Seity is a rare word for selfhood; the scoundrel sits inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Security can mean assurance or freedom from doubt, which is a sense of certainty.

clue.text: Hindu worshipper's object cut with thanks

indicators.note: something cut is trimmed short, so the word loses its final letter

blocks.note: sake is purpose or object, as in for the sake of
ta is informal British for thanks

explanation.surface: A devotee's sacred item, broken off, offered with gratitude.
explanation.walkthrough: Sake loses its last letter before ta is added.
explanation.definitionFit: A Sakta is a Hindu devotee of Shakti, the divine mother goddess, so a member of that sect of worshippers.

clue.text: Eire into shipping in mineral

indicators.note: shipping sends goods off and moves them around, so the letters are moved into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Ireland moving into the shipping trade for its minerals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shipping' reads as trade by sea, but it means sending the letters off to be rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Erionite is a fibrous zeolite, a naturally occurring crystalline mineral.

clue.text: Withholding power clear out press

indicators.note: withholding means keeping something back, so that letter is kept out of the word

blocks.note: P is the abbreviation for power
to purge is to clear out

explanation.surface: Keeping the electricity off while clearing out the printing press.
explanation.definitionFit: To press someone is to push or urge them strongly, so the verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: No longer flush dead fish

blocks.note: rud is an archaic word, used by Spenser, for red or ruddy
D is the abbreviation for dead

explanation.surface: A fish that has lost its rosy colour and died.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No longer' marks the word as archaic rather than signalling a deletion.
explanation.definitionFit: The rudd is a European freshwater fish of the carp family with reddish fins.

clue.text: Moral quality with Sturgeon's own group of bright stars

blocks.note: thew, usually plural, once meant a good quality or virtue
ain is Scots for own; Nicola Sturgeon is a Scottish politician

explanation.surface: A politician's own virtue among a constellation of stars.
explanation.walkthrough: Sturgeon is not a fish but Nicola Sturgeon, former First Minister of Scotland, so her word for own is Scots.
explanation.definitionFit: The Wain, or Charles's Wain, is the old name for the Plough asterism, seven bright stars in Ursa Major.

clue.text: Tell stories about being amongst your number

indicators.note: to be amongst others is to be surrounded by them, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: yr is an abbreviation for your
A is short for about, as in approximately
N stands for number

explanation.surface: Gossiping about a friend who has joined your group.
explanation.definitionFit: To yarn is to spin tales or chat at length, an informal verb for telling stories.

clue.text: Dancer may get into this academy, mostly late

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the word loses its last letter

blocks.note: uni is short for university, an academy
tardy means late

explanation.surface: A dancer can win a place at a school even when mostly late.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get into' reads as gaining admission to an academy; the dancer is literally getting into a garment.
explanation.definitionFit: A unitard is a one-piece skin-tight garment covering torso and legs, worn by dancers and gymnasts.

clue.text: Love poem being reinterpreted in a mass transit provision

indicators.note: reinterpreting something gives it a fresh reading, so its letters are put in a new arrangement
the rearranged letters are placed in, that is inside, the other piece

blocks.note: per means for each, as in twice a day
taken as written

explanation.surface: A love poem given a fresh reading on public transport.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearranged words sit inside a word meaning a, as in so much a head.
explanation.definitionFit: A people mover is an automated transit system, such as an airport shuttle, provided to carry large numbers of passengers.

clue.text: Little beast from centre of London borough turned over grass

indicators.note: something turned over is flipped, so the word is read from its end to its start

blocks.note: Barking is the main town of the London borough of Barking and Dagenham
a reed is a tall grass

explanation.surface: A small animal escaping from the middle of a London borough over the grass.
explanation.definitionFit: The barking deer, or muntjac, is a small deer known for its dog-like call, a little wild animal.

clue.text: Comb over for male in these

indicators.note: one thing given for another is a swap, so one letter group replaces another in the word

blocks.note: taken as written
he is a male pronoun
O is the cricket abbreviation for over

explanation.surface: A comb-over hairstyle on the men in question.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Comb over' looks like a single phrase about hair but splits into the definition and the substitute letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To tose (more often toze) is to tease out or card wool, which is combing it.

clue.text: First day in shopping centre gives you temper

indicators.note: the first pieces go in, that is inside, the word for the shopping centre

blocks.note: the town is where one goes to shop
one is the first number
D is the abbreviation for day

explanation.surface: Opening day at the mall puts you in a bad mood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Temper' looks like a noun for anger, but it is the verb meaning moderate.
explanation.definitionFit: To temper something is to moderate or soften it, which is what toning it down means.

clue.text: Difficulty that finishes off dense oaf in Washington

indicators.note: what finishes a word is its final letter, so only the end of the next word is kept

blocks.note: the rub is the difficulty, as in Hamlet's there's the rub
the final letter of dense

explanation.surface: A snag that defeats a thick lout in the American capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In Washington' marks the definition as American usage.
explanation.definitionFit: Rube is American slang for an unsophisticated country bumpkin, a clumsy oaf.

clue.text: Attention held by ceremonial salt

indicators.note: something held by another is clasped within it, so one piece sits inside the other

blocks.note: a state occasion is a ceremonial one
to give ear is to pay attention

explanation.surface: Formal ceremony commands attention, as does salt at table.
explanation.definitionFit: A stearate is a salt or ester of stearic acid, so a chemical salt.

clue.text: Starters for those arriving peckish at Seville?

definitions.text: Starters for those arriving peckish at Seville?

indicators.note: starters are what come first, so take the opening letter of each following word

blocks.note: the opening letters of the five words

explanation.surface: Little appetisers for hungry visitors to a Spanish city.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both definition and wordplay: starters names the opening letters and also the small dishes.
explanation.definitionFit: Tapas are small Spanish appetisers, typical bar snacks in Seville for anyone who is a little hungry.

clue.text: A case of going in quick, biblically grasping muscle

indicators.note: grasping something means closing around it, so the outer piece wraps the inner one

blocks.note: the quick and the dead in the Bible means the living and the dead
lat is short for latissimus dorsi, a back muscle

explanation.surface: A quick strike that grabs a muscle, as in some bible story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Case' is a grammatical case, not an example.
explanation.definitionFit: The allative is a grammatical case in Finnish and other languages expressing motion to or onto something.

clue.text: At St Andrews most trim fellows reversed destiny in year off

indicators.note: reversed means turned backwards, so the word for fellows is read end to start
off means removed or taken away, so the named letters are struck out of the word

blocks.note: dons are university fellows
taken as written
taken as written
Y is the abbreviation for year

explanation.surface: The neatest dons at a Scottish university have their fates altered during a gap year.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At St Andrews' marks the definition as Scots, not a location in the surface. Both the two letters and the year abbreviation are removed from destiny.
explanation.definitionFit: Snod is a Scots adjective for neat or trim, so the superlative means trimmest.

clue.text: Very joyful call over solitary double bass

blocks.note: V is the abbreviation for very
io is a Greek cry of joy or triumph
lone means solitary

explanation.surface: A happy shout above the sound of one lone bass instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: The violone is the large bass member of the viol family, the forerunner of the modern double bass.

clue.text: Soldiers get stuck into this protein quickly — flipping bad note

definitions.text: Soldiers get stuck into this protein

indicators.note: flipping something turns it round, so the word for bad is read backwards

blocks.note: vite is the musical direction for quickly
ill means bad
N stands for note

explanation.surface: Troops hurrying to tuck into protein, then a cross note about it.
explanation.walkthrough: Soldiers are strips of toast dipped into a boiled egg, not troops.
explanation.definitionFit: Vitellin is the main protein in egg yolk, which is what toast soldiers are dunked into.

clue.text: At Rome yes, better one speeding soul's delivery, supposedly

blocks.note: si is Italian for yes
neater means tidier, a better job

explanation.surface: In Rome, agreeing that a fast messenger makes a better courier of souls.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Speeding' here means hastening a soul on its way, not going too fast.
explanation.definitionFit: A sin-eater was paid to eat food over a corpse, supposedly taking on the dead person's sins and freeing the soul.

clue.text: Strangeness, and another with it being taken out of the earth

indicators.note: taken out means removed, so those letters are removed from the longer word

blocks.note: S is the physics symbol for the quantum number strangeness
another strangeness, an oddity
taken as written

explanation.surface: Something strange dug up out of the ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strangeness' in particle physics is a quantum number with the symbol S; 'another' is a second word for strangeness.
explanation.definitionFit: Soddy means made of or covered in sod, turf with soil, so earthy.

clue.text: Looking up enough said possibly dramatically for early coppers

indicators.note: in a down clue looking up means reading upwards, from bottom to top

blocks.note: sessa is a Shakespearean exclamation, possibly meaning enough said or be quiet

explanation.surface: Old-time policemen raising their eyes and saying no more in a theatrical way.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue looking up means read from the bottom. Coppers are coins, not police.
explanation.definitionFit: The as was an ancient Roman coin of bronze or copper, so the plural names early copper coins.

clue.text: In the thick of domestic, Bond's boss must step back

indicators.note: stepping back moves a letter one place later, so it is lifted out and set inside the rest

blocks.note: a domestic is a household servant, such as a maid
M is the head of MI6 in the James Bond stories

explanation.surface: In the middle of a household row, the spy chief has to retreat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Domestic' looks like a quarrel but is a servant; the letter for Bond's boss moves one place further back in it.
explanation.definitionFit: Amid is a preposition meaning in the middle of or surrounded by, the same as the phrase.

clue.text: Dodges down under succeeded with cotton fiber

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for succeeded
linters are the short fibres left on cotton seeds after ginning

explanation.surface: Someone ducking under a cotton thread.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Down under' means Australian usage, not beneath.
explanation.definitionFit: Slinter is Australian slang for a trick or dodge, so the plural means dodges.

clue.text: Growl once as fabulous creature that's hunted gets detailed

indicators.note: detailed is read as de-tailed, having its tail or final letter cut off

blocks.note: the Snark is the imaginary creature of Lewis Carroll's The Hunting of the Snark

explanation.surface: A mythical quarry snarling as it is cut down to size.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Detailed' means having the tail, the last letter, removed. 'Once' marks the word as archaic.
explanation.definitionFit: Snar is an obsolete verb meaning to snarl, so it is a former word for growl.

clue.text: Seize European scruff

blocks.note: to nap is an old slang word for seize or steal
E is the abbreviation for European

explanation.surface: Grabbing a scruffy man from the continent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scruff' looks like a scruffy person, but it is the back of the neck.
explanation.definitionFit: The scruff is the back of the neck, which is the anatomical nape.

clue.text: Tower's seat is to be announced north of River

blocks.note: TBA is the usual abbreviation for to be announced
R is the abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: Where someone in a tower will sit is yet to be revealed, upstream of a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tower' is one who tows, not a tall building. In a down clue north of means placed above.
explanation.definitionFit: A T-bar is a ski lift with a crossbar that tows skiers uphill, the bar acting as a perch.

clue.text: Let know familiar tenor must be left

blocks.note: T is the abbreviation for tenor
old means long known, familiar, as in an old friend

explanation.surface: Informing a well-known singer he has to go.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Must be left' sounds like a departure but places the tenor's letter on the left of the other piece.
explanation.definitionFit: To have told someone is to have informed them, the past tense of the phrase.

clue.text: Pleasant baron's naive bumbling

indicators.note: bumbling means muddled and clumsy, so the letters are jumbled into another order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An agreeable aristocrat's innocent blundering.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone non-abrasive is not harsh or grating in manner, hence agreeable.

clue.text: Rugby game's postponement finally accepted causing outcries, as before

indicators.note: finally points to the last part, so only the final letter of the word is used
something accepted is taken in, so that letter is placed inside the rugby game

blocks.note: sevens is rugby played with seven a side
the last letter of postponement

explanation.surface: Delaying a rugby match provokes protests.
explanation.walkthrough: 'As before' marks the definition as archaic; Spenser used steven for an outcry.
explanation.definitionFit: Steven is an old word for a voice or loud outcry, so the plural means outcries.

clue.text: Brown studies always with one in residence

indicators.note: the pieces go in the residence, so they sit inside its abbreviation

blocks.note: res is short for residence
ever means always
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Dark-panelled studies forever with someone living in the house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brown studies' looks like rooms with brown decor, but a brown study is a state of deep absorption.
explanation.definitionFit: A brown study is a daydreaming state, so brown studies are spells of dreamy musing.

clue.text: Hemingway, for example, casting central characters at first

indicators.note: casting off the central characters throws out the middle letters, leaving the two ends

blocks.note: Ernest is the first name of the writer Hemingway

explanation.surface: Hemingway casting the main parts in his first novel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At first' looks like a position signal but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Erst is an archaic adverb meaning formerly, originally, at first.
